extracted.intended_audience: media and publishing professionals (editors, journalists, industry analysts)
extracted.subtask_description: A news report describing the launch and content strategy of a new comedy-focused vertical (Vulture Comedy) created by New York magazine after acquiring Splitsider. It summarizes the types of content, platform distribution, and integration of acquired material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content sourced for Vulture Comedy
rubrics_metrics.description: Vulture Comedy features content gathered from topics interesting to readers of Vulture and Splitsider.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The vertical will combine subject matter that appealed to both sites, positioning itself as a hub for comedy-related topics across both audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Profiles of well-known comics
rubrics_metrics.description: Including profiles of well-known comics like Retta.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Long- and short-form profiles of established performers are a named content type for the vertical; profiles serve as flagship content to attract readers interested in personalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Podcast episode curation
rubrics_metrics.description: Popular episodes of Jesse David Fox’s Good One podcast will be featured.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site will surface and promote notable podcast episodes as part of its editorial mix, highlighting standout audio content for readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advice for budding comedians
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical guidance and how-to pieces aimed at emerging performers are explicitly part of the content slate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rankings of comedy specials
rubrics_metrics.description: A ranking of every Netflix comedy special.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listicles and ranked pieces (e.g., comprehensive rankings of streaming specials) are intended to be produced, indicating appetite for evaluative/curated editorial features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Splitsider columns on web videos
rubrics_metrics.description: Columns once found exclusively at Splitsider covering the best web videos of the week will run on the site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Established recurring columns from the acquired site will be migrated to the new vertical, preserving regular features and audience expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage of Twitter comedians and podcast commentary
rubrics_metrics.description: Twitter comedians and commentary on podcasts will also emerge on the channel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short-form social-media-driven reportage and commentary on audio media are components of the editorial remit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Republishing popular Splitsider content
rubrics_metrics.description: Popular content from Splitsider.com will appear on the channel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The vertical will incorporate and republish high-performing pieces from the acquired site to maintain continuity and leverage existing assets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-platform operation
rubrics_metrics.description: The new channel will operate across the New York website, Twitter and Facebook.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distribution strategy includes native publishing on the parent site plus social platforms to reach audiences where they consume comedy content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vulture Splitsider newsletter with exclusive content
rubrics_metrics.description: Will publish a Vulture Splitsider newsletter featuring exclusive content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Email newsletter is a named product for the vertical, promising exclusives to drive subscriptions and audience engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational integration following acquisition
rubrics_metrics.description: New York announced it had acquired Splitsider and would fold it into Vulture’s operations in May.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial and operational consolidation of an acquired comedy site into an existing entertainment vertical is part of the rollout strategy; integration of staff, columns, and content is implied.
